extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, research administrators, and applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH updates, policy reminders, resources, and brief guidance relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate experimental models
rubrics_metrics.description: "Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches, including New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), but emphasizes selecting models that enhance human relevance and translational potential and that are most appropriate to the specific research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 application format and be aware of linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants for PF5 should learn the required application format and be prepared for the possibility that applications may be split into linked awards after peer review and before Just-in-Time—use NIH overview resources to understand these procedural features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified by NIH for pilot DMS Plans (applicants should consult the issued format for the exact elements and structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH emphasizes reliability of biomedical research as foundational; applicants should incorporate replication and reproducibility practices into study design, and consider NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and the Replication and Reproducibility Initiative which aim to incentivize and institutionalize such efforts across the enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' scoring designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as ‘competitive but not discussed.’"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scoring policy (implemented as an emergency modification following a lapse in appropriations) means some applications deemed competitive may not be discussed in study section; applicants should understand this procedural outcome when interpreting review results and summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and reviewers should be aware of the consolidation’s intended effects—strengthening efficiency, competition, and transparency—and anticipate possible procedural and administrative changes to peer review processes resulting from centralization.
